meaning: A transcription step (invariant 16): the conclusion unfolds to the conjunction of the two premises, and it closes only because both premises are closed results. Refuting the weaker reading by the irrelevant-respect objection does not refute the strong-reading First Way: the objection is satisfiable together with the strong premises (finite model, AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-STRONG-PREMISES-COMPATIBLE-WITH-IRRELEVANT-RESPECT-OBJECTION) and leaves the conclusion derivable (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-STRONG-READING-YIELDS-UNMOVED-MOVER). Premise-free results verify the limits of this result: the same objection exposes the weaker reading's gap (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-IRRELEVANT-RESPECT-OBJECTION-EXPOSES-WEAK-GAP); the strong premises entail the weak premises (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-STRONG-PREMISES-ENTAIL-WEAK-PREMISES) and the absolute conclusion entails the relative one (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-ABSOLUTE-CONCLUSION-ENTAILS-RELATIVE), so an objection that falsifies a weaker premise or the relative conclusion would refute the strong form too.
